revision_rule.note: Clause 11.3.5 identifies both && and -> as short-circuiting, while 11.4.7 defines implication through !expression1 || expression2 and gives the controlling logical short-circuit condition.
The 2017 rule requires short-circuit evaluation for && and || only; it does not include logical implication (->) in the short-circuit mandate.
IEEE 1800-2012 clause 11.2.1 does not define constant built-in method calls or their elaboration-time evaluation.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define constant built-in method calls as constant-expression operands or require their elaboration-time evaluation.
IEEE 1800-2012 clause 11.2.1 has no constant built-in method-call category or eligibility rules.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no corresponding constant built-in method-call eligibility rules.
The 2012 operand list includes constant function and system-function calls but does not include constant built-in method calls.
The 2017 constant-expression operand list does not include constant built-in method calls, which are included by the 2023 expectation.
The 2012 table sizes an unsized constant number the same as integer, rather than specifying at least 32 bits.
The 2012 constant-argument list includes conversion, mathematical, and bit-vector functions, but not the later timescale functions or $sformatf; query-function exceptions remain.
The 2017 eligible constant-argument list covers conversion, mathematical, and bit-vector system functions, but not the 2023 additions for timescale functions and $sformatf.
The 2012 grammar permits a genvar identifier as a constant primary only within a genvar_expression, rather than throughout a loop generate construct.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits a genvar_identifier as a constant_primary only within a genvar_expression, rather than anywhere within a loop generate construct.
IEEE 1800-2012 set membership has bounded [low:high] ranges but no +/- absolute-tolerance range construct.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define the +/- absolute-tolerance form for an inside range.
The 2012 inside grammar supports expressions and bounded/open ranges but does not include +/- or +%- tolerance-range forms.
The 2017 inside grammar includes expression and ordinary or $-bounded ranges, but not the 2023 absolute and relative tolerance range forms.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no +%- relative-tolerance range construct for inside.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define the +%- relative-tolerance form for an inside range.
The 2017 short-circuit rule guarantees first-operand evaluation for && and ||, but does not include -> in that mandate.
The 2012 grammar and prose permit an expression as the tagged member value, whereas the 2023 rule requires a primary.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no inside tolerance ranges and therefore no tolerance-bound normalization, type, or truncation rules.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define inside tolerance ranges, so it has no normalization, result-type, or truncation rule for them.
